html:
Mongolia is a landlocked country of high grassland, mountains and desert between Russia and China. The map shows it from 1914, soon after it broke away from Qing China.

The steppe here was home to many nomad empires: the Xiongnu, the Turks, the Uyghurs and above all the Mongol Empire that Genghis Khan founded in 1206. After the Yuan fell in 1368 the Mongols went back to fighting among themselves. Tibetan Buddhism spread from the 1500s, and the Qing took the region in the 1600s.

When the Qing collapsed in 1911, Mongol nobles declared independence and enthroned the Bogd Khan, the country's leading Buddhist lama, as ruler. China reoccupied it in 1919. In 1921 Mongol revolutionaries with Soviet help drove out both the Chinese and a White Russian warlord, and in 1924 the Mongolian People's Republic was founded, the world's second communist state.

For seventy years Mongolia followed the Soviet line:

  • 1937 to 1939: purges killed tens of thousands, many of them monks, and nearly all monasteries were destroyed.
  • 1939: Soviet and Mongol forces beat Japan at Khalkhin Gol.
  • 1961: Mongolia joined the United Nations.

Peaceful protests in 1990 ended one-party rule. Mongolia has been a multiparty democracy since its 1992 constitution, with an economy built on herding and mining.
sum: Mongolia is a landlocked country of high grassland, mountains and desert between Russia and China. The map shows it from 1914, soon after it broke away from Qing China.
